## How To Use This

Every pain point below is one I met, with what was built to fix it. Each one
is short so it can be lifted into a slide or said aloud. The decision numbers
(D51 and so on) point into `plan/decisions.md` for the full reasoning, if I am
asked to go deeper.

**The work in numbers** (17 September to 2 October 2026): 321 commits in 16
days; 187 recorded decisions; 90 defects logged and fixed by 1 October;
about 1,050 automated tests; about 36,000 lines of Python. One person
specified, directed, tested and ran all of it, using AI coding agents, and
learned SQL, Python and R along the way.

---

## 1. The Core Problem

- **Every pull was hand-built SQL.**
  Each research question meant writing Cosmos SQL by hand, then moving the
  results into a project database by hand.
  *Fix:* Gen1, my first generator on the VM, wrote the SQL from a YAML
  description of the pull. Telescope replaced it: pulls are assembled from
  reusable recipes, checked against a data dictionary, and run by a program
  that writes its own SQL.

- **Getting more data on patients I already had meant pulling them again.**
  To add information about, say, all Crohn's patients, I had to wait for the
  whole cohort to be found again before anything new came back.
  *Fix:* a patient list can be uploaded as the starting cohort. 1.28 million
  Crohn's patients went up in about two and a half minutes, and the new
  tables were built from them directly.

- **Big pulls were unreliable.** Gen1 warned past 80 million rows, and one
  dropped connection lost everything.
  *Fix:* pulls are planned into sessions, batches and chunks, each recorded as
  it finishes, so a failure costs one piece, not the whole pull.

- **Gen1 had grown fragile.** One script did parsing, SQL, execution,
  reporting and file copying.
  - It chose which SQL to run by searching text, so `PKTable` matched
    `PKTable2` and that table was dropped and refilled on every run (D31).
  - It read row counts out of column names (D32).
  - A misspelt `dedup_key` silently turned deduplication off (D28).
  - A test row limit applied to every patient table, so a chained cohort
    became "500 patients and then 500 of their events" (D29).

  *Fix:* rebuilt from scratch, not ported (D2). Each of Gen1's hard-won
  behaviours became a tested contract, and its architecture was dropped.

---

## 2. A Locked-Down Windows Machine

- **Only the packages already installed.** Nothing can be added.
  *Fix:* standard library plus the VM's own list. The Mac runs the VM's exact
  Python and package versions, so code is tested on what it will meet.

- **No web pages.** The VM blocks localhost pages and local HTML files.
  *Fix:* the browser tool was retired for one tkinter app, Author and Run,
  identical on the Mac and the VM (D44, D92, D93, D112).

- **Running a pull from the app crashed at once** (`0xC0000142`), and a shell
  could not be counted on.
  *Fix:* each pull opens its own console running Python directly, closed only
  by typing `exit` (D68).

- **Windows' "check if a process is alive" kills it instead.**
  *Fix:* a heartbeat file marks a running pull (D67).

- **A click froze a finished pull.** Clicking a console window pauses all its
  output (QuickEdit), so a done pull looked hung.
  *Fix:* Telescope turns QuickEdit off (D143).

- **A pull died with exit code 1 and left no reason.**
  *Fix:* the log now keeps any traceback and where a native crash happened, so
  the next one explains itself.

- **The network share refuses to replace a file that anything has open.** The
  window showing progress was blocking the pull from saving its progress.
  *Fix:* saves wait and retry for up to five minutes, then stop with a
  message saying who usually holds the file; the window reads less often
  (D153, D154, D175).

- **No database to test against.** Nothing on the Mac can reach Cosmos.
  *Fix:* fake databases that fail the way real ones do (mid-batch errors,
  partial landings), and every build checked by me on the VM.

---

## 3. How Cosmos And SQL Server Actually Behave

- **Temporary tables vanish when the connection drops.**
  *Fix:* the central design idea. Each part of a pull runs inside one held
  connection, and all SQL is written before connecting (D36).

- **The server's name changes on every connection.**
  *Fix:* captured fresh each time (D37).

- **Cosmos cannot reach back into the project database.**
  *Fix:* uploads travel through the client, in fast bulk batches (D38, D54).

- **SQL Server caps an `INSERT ... VALUES` at 1,000 rows, and CSV values
  arrived as text.**
  *Fix:* bound parameters, and CSVs converted to typed parquet (D38, D54).

- **The login cannot see table metadata.**
  *Fix:* rows are counted, never read from metadata (D33).

- **Cosmos is rebuilt monthly.** A pull that spans a rebuild mixes two
  populations.
  *Fix:* refresh detection, and a refresh means a full re-pull (D51). Later,
  a false alarm: Cosmos runs on several copies made minutes apart, so a
  reconnection looked like a refresh. A refresh is now a move of more than a
  day (D183).

- **Pulls running side by side overwrote each other's temporary tables.**
  *Fix:* every pull gets its own prefix, numbered on a clash (D50).

- **The project database filled up** (20 GB cap), stopping pulls while other
  databases stood empty.
  *Fix:* a tool to see and clear space (D133); each pull is given the
  database with the most room (D164); a finished pull's tables are dropped
  once safely packaged (D165); and, agreed next, each table group is packaged
  and emptied as it finishes, so a pull needs room only for its largest group
  (D177).

- **Pulls sharing a database dropped each other's tables.**
  *Fix:* every project table carries its pull's prefix (D163).

- **Sign-ins expire after 10 hours**, so long sessions failed partway.
  *Fix:* the connection is reopened per table group, with one retry on an
  expired sign-in (D176).

- **One very long connection per cohort.**
  *Fix:* table groups, each on its own connection (D134).

---

## 4. Silent Data Errors

The worst kind: the pull says "done" and the data is wrong.

- **SQL errors were being swallowed.** An error in a later statement of a
  batch read as "no more results", so IBD Ancestry's White controls (1.2
  million patients found) landed nothing and were marked done.
  *Fix:* every error now fails its step, a missing row count is an error, and
  every server message goes to the log (D151). A scan of every earlier pull
  then found two more silent losses, one about 9 million rows short (D152).

- **A "resume" feature deleted the batches it claimed to keep**, and its test
  passed, because the test checked the wrong thing.
  *Fix:* removed (D46). Since then every bug fix gets a test of the
  *outcome*, what data ends up where, confirmed to fail with the bug put
  back.

- **The race split was never applied**: the Black and White cohorts were the
  same patients. Found on the first dry run on the VM (D59).

- **Chunked runs pulled only the first chunk.** Most of each batch missing,
  silently.

- **Every cohort ran in every session**: 1,120 SQL files where 168 were
  right, with the wrong population able to land.

- **An option that quietly left rows out** (`include_other`).
  *Fix:* retired; the batches together are always the whole cohort (D76).

- **A stratification with no levels** made every table vanish.
  *Fix:* now an error naming it (D84).

- **A database switch read the wrong database** and labelled it as the other
  (D39).

- **Fact tables joined to nothing** would have pulled every row in Cosmos.
  *Fix:* an error at validation (D129).

- **A copied template still joined another pull's cohort.**
  *Fix:* an error naming what the pull actually makes (D178).

- **Nullability became a hidden filter.** A column marked "never empty" added
  an `IS NOT NULL` that turned an optional join into a required one, dropping
  rows.
  *Fix:* only the safe dictionary corrections applied; new columns to be left
  optional (D172).

- **A Celiac pull returned Crohn's patients.** I caught it reading the data:
  the file sent had the wrong code.

---

## 5. A Data Dictionary I Could Not Fully Trust

- **Types in the dictionary were wrong**, and SQL Server's error named no
  column.
  *Fix:* every dictionary page screenshotted and checked column by column;
  templates no longer carry types at all, the dictionary fills them in at
  export (784 copies removed), so one correction fixes every pull (D114,
  D115, D130, D160).

- **The dictionary listed a column Cosmos does not have**, found after an
  11-minute query.
  *Fix:* an audit button on the VM compares the dictionary with Cosmos, and
  each session checks its columns exist before building anything (D155,
  D156, D161).

- **Some dictionary columns exist only in Epic's reporting tool**, not the
  database.
  *Fix:* only database columns are recorded (D116).

- **Some "facts" about how Cosmos tables relate were convention or AI
  paraphrase, never checked by a query.**
  *Fix:* every fact is graded seen (on a dictionary page), counted (a query
  ran) or said, and only the first two are trusted.

---

## 6. Mistakes While Authoring

- **SQL typos showed up only at run time**, hours in. Infant RSV had nine
  (wrong aliases, a misspelt column, unjoined tables).
  *Fix:* every alias and column checked at validation and as each line is
  typed; renaming an alias rewrites its lines (D118).

- **"Valid" in the app, failing in the runner.** The saved file differed from
  what was checked.
  *Fix:* both read the same saved file; the saving bugs fixed (D103).

- **Hand-edited YAML.**
  *Fix:* an app with dropdowns, a picker that offers only tables that fit,
  messages shown at the field they concern (D96, D169). Errors suggest the
  fix and never guess what I meant (D45).

- **Names that misled.** The dry run looked required; "include other" read as
  "lump the rest"; a batch's `column` did not read as a requirement.
  *Fix:* renamed: Preview SQL, Validation Output, `required_column` (D71,
  D76, D80).

- **Which pull is this window showing?**
  *Fix:* both halves named in the title, one dropdown at a time (D166).

- **A database field that the runner overrode.**
  *Fix:* agreed: a "Specify Project DB" box, off by default (D179).

- **Row keys and deduplication typed by hand.**
  *Fix:* agreed: picked from the table's columns (D186).

---

## 7. Not Knowing What A Long Pull Was Doing

- **A pull printed nothing for hours**, so slow looked the same as hung.
  *Fix:* every phase, table and upload says when it starts and ends, timed;
  the table in flight is shown (D136, D166).

- **A finished pull looked stopped**, because only the first table's count was
  recorded.
  *Fix:* every table's own row count, in the log, the manifest and the
  Status tab (D137).

- **Why did it stop?**
  *Fix:* each pull ends as finished, finished with errors, stopped by user or
  stopped with errors, and the full manifest is viewable with errors in red
  (D140, D144).

- **Duplicates or real data?** Celiac's 1.15 million diagnoses looked like a
  deduplication failure; they were 93 codes per patient.
  *Fix:* every table records rows per patient (median, 90th percentile, max)
  (D157).

- **Not knowing a pull's size until it had run.**
  *Fix:* agreed: a Count button that asks Cosmos first and builds nothing
  (D181).

---

## 8. Starting Over After Every Failure

- **A failure meant restarting the pull.**
  *Fix:* a manifest records every step's status; a failed batch is retried
  alone; chosen sessions can be re-pulled, with a case bringing its controls
  (D9 to D14, D52, D158).

- **One failure could lose finished work.**
  *Fix:* "a bird in hand": each cohort is committed as it lands (D55).

- **Random samples changed every run.**
  *Fix:* deterministic hashing, so a result can be looked at again (D60).

- **One pull at a time.**
  *Fix:* several pulls side by side, each with its own console, lock and run
  folder (D57, D67).

---

## 9. Getting Data To Clients

- **Clients are not coders.**
  *Fix:* Artifacts: parquet files, a plain-language `contents.md` (each
  table's grain, how its patients were chosen, every column's type and
  meaning), load scripts in R and Python, and a how-to (D72 to D75).

- **Large files were slow to open.**
  *Fix:* a parquet viewer that reads only the page on screen (D146).

- **No safe place for backups** (no Git LFS; parquets kept out of GitLab).
  *Fix:* a backup to a second drive, taken just before packaging replaces a
  pull (D149).

- **What to hand over.**
  *Fix:* each pull's folder is the deliverable, with only the client's
  utilities (D148).

- **Tools mistaken for the vendor's.**
  *Fix:* a credit line on every window (D145).

---

## 10. Building It Alone, With AI

- **Learning SQL, Python and R from nothing** while building it.

- **Design documents drifted apart** (seven of them).
  *Fix:* three documents, one job each: what it is, why, and what is left. A
  fact lives in one place (D47).

- **An AI gave a reason for a rule that never had one**, and I acted on it.
  *Fix:* an append-only decision log. Every choice has its recorded reason,
  and reversed decisions keep theirs (D1 onward).

- **Tests that passed while the bug was live.**
  *Fix:* the outcome-test rule (Section 4).

- **Several AI sessions working at once.**
  *Fix:* a fixed cycle: the AI answers each topic in the task list and I
  decide; decisions are written and committed before any code; fixes are
  built in an agreed order, one commit each; results are discussed before the
  docs change.
